title: 3886. Sum of Sortable Integers

examples.explanation: For n = 3, possible divisors are 1 and 3. For k = 1: each subarray has one element. No rotation can sort the array. For k = 3: the single subarray [3, 1, 2] can be rotated once to produce [1, 2, 3], which is sorted. Only k = 3 is sortable. Hence, the answer is 3.

For n = 3, possible divisors are 1 and 3. For k = 1: each subarray has one element. No rotation can sort the array. For k = 3: the single subarray [7, 6, 5] cannot be rotated into non-decreasing order. No k is sortable. Hence, the answer is 0.
For n = 2, possible divisors are 1 and 2. Since [5, 8] is already sorted, every divisor is sortable. Hence, the answer is 1 + 2 = 3.

hints: First, observe that k must divide n, since the array is partitioned into subarrays of length k. Iterate over all divisors of n.
Let s be the sorted version of the array. For each divisor k, check every block [i, i+k).
A block can be rotated to match its sorted counterpart if the sorted segment s[i..i+k-1] appears as a cyclic rotation of nums[i..i+k-1].
You can test this by checking whether the sorted segment exists inside two concatenated copies of the block. If all blocks satisfy this, then k is sortable.
